figs.title: Stress components on a cube
figs.caption: Each σ_ij acts on the face with outward normal e_i and points along e_j. A component is positive on a positive face in a positive direction, or on a negative face in a negative direction, and moment balance gives σ_ij = σ_ji.

figs.title: Reynolds transport theorem
figs.caption: A material volume coincides with a fixed control volume at time t and has moved slightly by t + dt. The rate of change of ρφ in the material volume equals the storage rate inside the control volume plus the net flux ρφ(v·n) out through its surface.

figs.title: Bimaterial strip under heating
figs.caption: Heated freely, the higher α layer would grow more than the lower α layer. Bonded, they share one interface strain, so the strip curves with the higher α layer on the convex side and bends toward the lower α layer.

figs.title: Thick cylinder stresses through the wall
figs.caption: For internal pressure p and b/a = 2, the hoop stress peaks at the bore at 5p/3 and falls to 2p/3 at the outer surface, while the radial stress rises from −p to 0. The hoop stress averages pa/(b − a) across the wall, which is the thin-wall value.

figs.title: Neo-Hookean versus linear in uniaxial stretch
figs.caption: Both models share the initial slope 3μ at λ = 1. The neo-Hookean nominal stress μ(λ − λ⁻²) softens toward slope μ in tension and stiffens sharply in compression as λ approaches zero.
